intro: Lesson 26: The gut, peristalsis and absorption in the villus. To understand how the alimentary canal moves food and how the small intestine is adapted for absorption

picture.alt: A diagram of villi in the small intestine
picture.draw: Draw and label: Homework, lesson 26: Draw and label the alimentary canal with the job of each organ .

questions.q: Put in order: stomach, oesophagus, small intestine, mouth, large intestine.
questions.a: Mouth, oesophagus, stomach, small intestine, large intestine.
questions.model: Start where food enters: mouth. Swallowed down the oesophagus. Mixed with acid in the stomach. Digested and absorbed in the small intestine. Water absorbed in the large intestine.

questions.a: Waves of muscle contraction that push food along the gut.

questions.q: Name the vessel in a villus that absorbs fatty acids.
Core: Label a villus and write three adaptations with how each helps absorption.
questions.a: Thin wall one cell thick: short diffusion distance; rich capillary network: maintains the gradient; microvilli: large surface area; lacteal for lipids.
questions.model: Teacher labels the first: 'Wall one cell thick: short distance for digested molecules to diffuse into the blood.'

questions.q: Extend: Coeliac disease flattens villi. Explain why people with it may lose weight. [3 marks]
questions.a: Flattened villi reduce surface area (1); less absorption of digested food (1); fewer nutrients and less energy reach the body (1).

questions.q: Stretch: Explain why the small intestine absorbs glucose by both diffusion and active transport.
questions.a: Diffusion while the gut has more glucose than the blood; active transport takes up the rest against the gradient.

questions.q: Digested food is absorbed mainly in the...
Big question: how does food get from your plate into your blood?
questions.a: It is digested into small molecules and absorbed across the villi of the small intestine into the blood.
